questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Kigali?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Rwanda is Kigali.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Rwanda?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Rwanda article.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Rwanda on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Rwanda on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Rwanda?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Rwanda on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Rwanda article.

questions.proof: Rwanda is bordered by Uganda to the north, Tanzania to the east, Burundi to the south, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the west.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Rwanda about 26,338 square kilometres; Eswatini about 17,364 square kilometres; Mauritius about 2,040 square kilometres; Comoros about 2,034 square kilometres.
